newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- State transport concern, Transnet, has approved a record capital budget of almost 1.5 billion rand for South Africa's seven commercial ports in 1997/98.
- Del Monte Royal Foods' earnings fell 34 percent to 40 million rand in the six months to May after sharply reduced earnings in its European canned fruit and fruit juice operations.

- The trade and industry department's standing advisory committee on company law has called for comment on "N" shares, which could lead to changes in the Companies Act and Johannesburg Stock Exchange rules.

- Public Protector Selby Baqwa has asked Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma to substantiate statements she made on the cost of medicines and the use of generic medicines in South Africa in support of medicines control legislation.
- Forbes Group is prepared to pay 660 million rand, a premium of 43 percent, for the 90.06 percent stake it does not own in London insurance broker Nelson Hurst.
- More than 8,000 mineworkers allied to the National Union of Mineworkers marched on Wednesday to the East Driefontein mine offices owned by Gold Fields to force pay claims.
- The Reserve Bank will sign a $1.5 billion syndicated loan with a group of foreign banks in London next week, Governor Chris Stals said.

- The department of trade and industry announced that the advisory committee on company law is seeking opinion on "N" share schemes and black empowerment moves could be dealt a blow if the committee recommends that these are declared illegal, merchant bankers say.

- The weak gold price is a factor, but a survey of economists shows they believe the prime lending rate will fall by 50 basis points to 19.75 percent in September, and by another 50 points by year-end.
- Stock market indices around the world, including on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, have been setting new records.
- A car hijacking suspect, released after a bungled indentity parade last year, is now being held in connection with the killing last month of a Sandton businessman.
- An eight million rand project to house Johannesburg's homeless will be unveiled on Thursday when Deputy President Thabo Mbeki launches a two billion rand inner-city renewal plans.
